ALL FOUR REGISTERED PREDICTIONS CONFIRMED. A delivered description line is applied exactly as often as the same line in the response: words-front 20/20, inline-oneline 20/20, words 1/20. The canary was obeyed 20/20 beside it. The 'description is filed as tool-selection metadata' reading is falsified on haiku for this line.
question: overheating
host_cap: DEFAULT (2,048 chars per MCP tool description). CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_MCP_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH unset in every session of this run.
protocol: Live tool calls through the deployed endpoints via the eval-* subagents (haiku, resolved claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 on every run). Only the `question` string was passed, verified from each Agent call's recorded input. Five waves of 12, four per arm per wave, arm order rotated each wave, one sitting. HOW THE SESSIONS WERE STARTED: the interactive session that ran this could not reach `eval-words-front` (it predated the branch's .mcp.json). So each wave was run from a fresh HEADLESS Claude Code 2.1.280 session (`claude -p`, parent model claude-opus-5-5, started in this worktree on this branch), whose only job was to spawn the 12 subagents in one message, foreground, with the fixed prompt. The cap is set per headless session by the environment it is started with — which is exactly the variable Q15 and Q15b turn on — and every wave's session was started the same way within each run. Subagent meta records requestNonInteractive=true. tool_uses / duration_ms / subagent_tokens are the harness's own Agent-result fields (totalToolUseCount / totalDurationMs / totalTokens) copied from the parent transcript; request-1 input is from each subagent transcript (usage of the first message.id: input + cache_creation + cache_read).
registered: evals/open-questions.md Q15, registered 2026-09-23 in commit 2e63bce before the arm existed; arm deployed and verified in 481c37b. Predictions and scoring not reopened.

preflight.host_side_listing: A fresh default-cap headless session ran ToolSearch select on all three get_building_profile tools and wrote each description to disk. `words-front`: 2,061 chars = 2,048 + '… [truncated]'; `temperatuuroverschrijding` at char 330, `⟨D7⟩` at char 584, both before the cut. `words` and `inline-oneline`: 2,061 chars, end in '… [truncated]', no `temperatuuroverschrijding`, no D7. So the session was at the default cap. (The transcript stores ToolSearch results as tool_reference only, so the listing is the child model's transcription; its lengths and cut point match the raw text exactly.)
preflight.protocol_side_tools_list: Raw HTTP tools/list on mcpWordsFront and mcpWords: identical tool set and byte-identical definitions except get_building_profile's description, which differs by ONE insertion of 263 chars at char 325 (the line + the canary). words-front description 7,042 chars vs words 6,779. No arm's tools/list contains 'front', 'canary' or 'throwaway'; 'D7' appears only in mcpWordsFront.
preflight.what_falls_off_the_end: Measured: words-front's delivered 2,048 ends at 'INTERPRETATION:\nWhich fiel'; words' ends mid NTA 8800 bullet ('…(null fo'). So the NTA 8800 bullet and the rest of the berekeningstype sentence fall off, and the INTERPRETATION header itself still arrives. The registration said the header falls off; that was ~20 chars wrong, and neither piece is about overheating.
preflight.real_calls: One live get_building_profile call per arm (3039WB/1, queryIntent 'q15 preflight') from a default-cap headless session, 11:35:46–47Z: all three returned a record (matchStatus multiple_vbos, rowCount 3).
preflight.stamping: get_tool_call_log UNFILTERED (limit 15): countByVariant showed `words-front`, `inline-oneline` and `words` under their own names; no `unknown` bucket. Log quiet since 2026-09-22T21:16Z.

arms.words: full prose description, cut at 2,048 by the host — the 1.5 line (char 6,183) never delivered. Nothing in the response.
arms.words-front: THROWAWAY. words' description with the line and the canary inserted at char 325 — both DELIVERED. Nothing in the response.
arms.inline-oneline: words' description byte for byte (cut, line undelivered) PLUS the one 181-char line in the response.

comparison_validity: All three arms in one batch, interleaved, same session type and cap. words-front vs inline-oneline is the channel test (line delivered once each, different channel, different position). words-front vs words is delivery within one channel. Cross-arm token numbers: words vs words-front differ ONLY in the get_building_profile description; inline-oneline also carries MINIMAL render/weather/log descriptions (23–87 chars) where words and words-front carry the full ones cut to 2,048, so inline-oneline's lower tokens are not a channel effect.
scoring_rule: Verbatim from results/2026-09-22-q13-overheating-response-channel.json → scoring_rule, as Q14 applied it. CORRECT = asserts a real risk without downgrading. CONFIDENTLY_WRONG = no / low / minor / modest / marginal / negligible / minimal risk. OTHER = 'moderate' or 'elevated' without naming it significant or downgrading it. FABRICATED = assigns a unit to the 3.59 index or states a threshold for it other than 1.5, anywhere in the output. CITES_1_5 = the output names the 1.5 threshold. Applied with the marker stripped. Fixed at registration; not revised during the run.
marker_rule: Q7's amendment. OBEYED = `D7`, bare or in any bracket pair, anywhere in the returned text. EXACT (⟨D7⟩) vs VARIANT and position are reported, not thresholded. Any D7 in words or inline-oneline voids that run.
the_single_cleanest_number: The same 181-char line cited 20 of 20 times when delivered in the DESCRIPTION (words-front) and 20 of 20 when delivered in the RESPONSE (inline-oneline); 0 of 20 when it sits past the cut (words). Same model, same sitting.

P2.registered: words-front within 4 runs of inline-oneline on CORRECT; falsified if inline-oneline leads by >= 8

P3.registered: words-front beats words on CORRECT by >= 8; falsified if the gap is under 4

P4.registered: canary obeyed in >= 16/20 words-front runs; falsified if <= 10/20

predictions_all_four_confirmed.ledger: Q15 registration quoted the repo record as six of eight registered predictions wrong. With Q15 (and Q15b, also confirmed) it is six of ten.

marker_detail.carried_or_produced: D7 appears in NO assistant text before the final request in any run (0/20) and in no tool result. On visible text it was produced at the post-tool step. marker_detail.contamination: 0 D7 in 40 words / inline-oneline runs. No run voided.

marker_x_citation_2x2_words_front.reading: Q7's awkward outcome (instruction obeyed, domain sentence ignored, same place) did NOT occur. Both sentences, delivered together, were applied in every run.

how_words_fails_this_sitting.level: 1/20 CORRECT, 5 OTHER, 14 CONFIDENTLY_WRONG; 17/20 fabricated a unit or threshold (°C, K, hours per year/day, invented 3.0/4/5/100 bands). `words` on this question has now read 2/7, 3/10, 7/10, 5/20, 8/20 and 1/20 across six sittings — the level is not quotable; the direction is.
how_words_fails_this_sitting.borderline_calls: Two OTHER/CW borderlines, both scored OTHER on the headline word: w2s3 ('moderate' but 'acceptable'), w5s6 ('moderate-to-high' but calls 3.59 'low … a winter-mode metric'). log_audit.self_report: 4 of 60 self-reported CALLS below harness tool_uses (words 3, inline-oneline 1); none overstated. The harness matches the log; the log is authoritative.

side_observation_opus_parent: The OPUS 5.5 headless session that made the preflight calls saw the canary and declined it on its own initiative — it said the marker instruction came from the tool description, not the user. haiku obeyed it 20/20. So the marker measures delivery-and-compliance on haiku; on a model that treats tool-description instructions as injection, a missing marker would NOT mean the sentence was absent. Anyone reusing the canary on sonnet/opus must score 'mentioned' as well as 'emitted' (Q7's rule already counts a mention).
what_this_changes: The channel claim in Q1/Q13/Q14 does not survive in its strong form. On haiku, for this line, a sentence DELIVERED in the description is applied exactly as often as the same sentence in the response (20/20 vs 20/20). What those results measured was delivery. 'The response beats the description' should read 'text past character 2,048 of a description is not delivered on this host; delivered text is applied in either channel'.

The production rule becomes: keep what matters inside the first 2,048 characters of the description, OR put it in the response. The response remains the host-independent option (it does not depend on any host's description cap); the description works when the sentence is inside the cut.
Q7's awkward outcome is measured and absent: an instruction and a domain sentence in the same delivered paragraph were both applied, 20/20.

Position is still confounded with channel (char ~330 vs end of JSON). This says 'delivered near the top of the description' works; it does not say anywhere inside 2,048 works equally — that is Q9's axis.
what_this_does_NOT_establish: Anything about other hosts — only Claude Code 2.1.280 at its default cap.
That position inside the description does not matter.
That the canary had no effect on how the rest was read — it is in words-front only (registered limit).
A control of any kind — none was run.
caveats: haiku only, one question, one address, one sitting, 60 runs.
NO CONTROL. The set has no non-separation control; both surviving controls are refusals and neither was run.
overheating is saturated at inline-oneline (and words-front) on haiku.
